text:
A fruit that shares a name with a color is **lime** (or **orange**, **lemon**, **cherry**, **plum**, etc.).

Here are three creative ways to transform your leftover salmon, baby potatoes, dill, pasta, and garlic into new, appealing dishes:

1. **Creamy Dill-Garlic Salmon & Potato Pasta**
   Sauté minced garlic in olive oil until fragrant. Add halved baby potatoes and a splash of water, covering to steam until tender. Flake the leftover salmon into the pan. Toss in cooked pasta, then stir in a generous amount of chopped fresh dill. Finish with a splash of pasta water and a squeeze of lime (or lemon) to create a light, herbaceous sauce that coats everything without needing heavy cream.

2. **Warm Salmon and Potato Salad with Dill Vinaigrette**
   Boil the baby potatoes until soft, then slice them. Toss the warm potatoes with flaked salmon, cooked pasta, and plenty of fresh dill. Whisk together olive oil, garlic (minced or pressed), lemon juice, salt, and pepper to make a simple vinaigrette. Pour over the warm ingredients so they absorb the flavors, creating a hearty, no-cook meal that highlights the freshness of the dill.

3. **Garlic-Dill Salmon Potato Skillet with Pasta Garnish**
   Pan-sear the salmon fillets until crispy on the outside. In the same pan, sauté sliced garlic and halved baby potatoes until golden and cooked through. Remove the salmon, then toss in cooked pasta to warm it up in the flavorful pan juices. Flake the salmon back in, garnish heavily with fresh dill, and serve immediately. This dish offers a mix of textures: crispy salmon, tender potatoes, and soft pasta.
